requirements.requirement: VyOS node1 routes traffic between lan-a and lan-b with appropriately scoped forwarding.
requirements.summary: Node1 has addresses and connected routes on both private LANs with forwarding enabled and bidirectional subnet-scoped firewall rules. Hosts on each LAN successfully reached the opposite LAN, forwarding counters recorded traffic, and the routing configuration survived node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 is the control plane and node3/node4 are Ready worker members of one Kubernetes cluster.
requirements.summary: The final recovered cluster lists exactly node2 as Ready control-plane and node3/node4 as Ready workers, with their private-LAN addresses as Internal-IP values. Core system and validation pods were also Ready after all restarts.

requirements.requirement: Kubernetes control and data traffic use the private LAN interfaces rather than the management network.
requirements.summary: The API is advertised and bound at node2's lan-a address, worker agents target that private endpoint, node Internal-IP values are private, and every Flannel VXLAN endpoint is explicitly local to enp8s0 on the appropriate private LAN. Route selection between control plane and workers also uses enp8s0 through node1.

requirements.requirement: Cross-LAN pod networking, cluster DNS, and ClusterIP services work from pods on all three Kubernetes nodes.
requirements.summary: After all node restarts, pods on node2, node3, and node4 each resolved cluster DNS, reached the ClusterIP service, and directly reached every pod IP, including paths crossing the two private LANs. The service retained three healthy endpoints.

overall_summary: All material public outcomes are satisfied in the final recovered state. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for every managed node: node1 (cmd-4345a72544ca41fd, cmd-17e4dc29cbc04eb4, cmd-648acb41db944a2e, cmd-5d88e3de5f1f4908, cmd-0d9627933d754816), node2 (cmd-4766697cbe6f40ec, cmd-a9dbde91ea754abf, cmd-50ab6a596b4b42c0, cmd-dbddaa27de224edd, cmd-cc402dd99e934771), node3 (cmd-9d46410dab72436e, cmd-e68bd55c8a7846dc, cmd-2ee74e6de0354ae1, cmd-77e395c8cb194208, cmd-fc999910c1224a47), and node4 (cmd-723fac10d86e45ee, cmd-8a9e6a58065c4789, cmd-71d17486363449ab, cmd-3b87ae7e397b4e36, cmd-19ca42a0198c4a54). Each has a healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster evidence; the fixed after-executor boot identities independently agree.
limitations: Management-network non-use is demonstrated through private Internal-IP values, API bindings, Flannel underlay interfaces, and route selection rather than packet capture. The final snapshots also show worker kubelet port 10250 bound to all addresses, so the evidence does not establish whether management-interface access to that authenticated listener is filtered (global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets, global:after_executor:node4:listening-sockets).

The first comprehensive check immediately after node2 restarted encountered transient 502 errors while worker reverse tunnels reconnected (cmd-95043db9c6d44be4). A focused retry and the final all-node test succeeded shortly afterward (cmd-9cecfde2877849c0, cmd-cc402dd99e934771), supporting recovery but not a precise recovery-time bound.
Lifecycle snapshots are bounded inventories and do not enumerate every persistent file or firewall detail; hygiene conclusions therefore also rely on the complete captured command trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two unnecessary mutations were identified. The initial VyOS transaction created rule 5 with an unrestricted accept action after its intended state qualifiers were rejected; it was committed briefly, weakening forwarding isolation, but was fully deleted and saved in the immediately following corrective transaction. The K3s server installation unnecessarily selected write-kubeconfig-mode 0644, leaving the administrative kubeconfig readable by all local users; no reversion is evidenced. Other mutations—private routes, scoped routing rules, K3s installation, the validation service, and mandatory restarts—had clear task or evidence roles. Final snapshots show no failed services, package damage, or unexplained temporary-file residue.
